newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Seven survive as 21 die in Colombia chopper attack.
newsitem.headline: Seven survive as 21 die in Colombia chopper attack.

text.p: Seven people, initially feared dead, survived when the helicopter in which they were flying was shot down by leftist rebels in an oil-producing region of eastern Colombia, military sources said on Monday.

The army originally said all on board -- 24 soldiers and four civilian crew members -- died when the Russian-made Mi-17 chopper went down near the town of Arauquita in Arauca province Sunday. But by Monday army sources reduced the final death toll to 20 soldiers and one civilian.

"We have confirmed four soldiers survived and we have three surviving crew members," said army chief Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, in Arauca to head the operation to recover the bodies of the dead and track down the National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels blamed for the attack.
"The area has now been secured and air reinforcements have been brought in," he added.
President Ernesto Samper condemned Monday the incident as an "act of terror and cowardice".

"Some subversives are afraid of peace and of sitting down at the negotiating table to achieve what they think can achieve by the blind use of weapons," he said, referring to his plans to launch a new peace process to end Colombia's three-decade-old guerrilla uprising.

Political analysts believe those plans are now following a spate of rebel assaults in the last three weeks. In comments to reporters Monday afternoon, Gen. Harold Bedoya, the head of the Colombian armed forces, called for the nation to unite and "talk less about making peace with the guerrillas".
Bedoya, a hawk, is at the forefront of calls to defeat the rebels by military might.

The four surviving soldiers made their way to a military post late on Sunday night, two of them were suffering from extensive burns. Three crew members were discovered alive by an army ground patrol near the crash site on Monday, Bonett told reporters.

Images broadcast by local media Monday night showed the remains of the dead soldiers in body bags being taken out of a helicopter at an airbase in Arauca. The corpses were understood to be badly charred after the downed helicopter exploded as it hit the ground.

The ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla force set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, shot the helicopter down as it flew over the site where guerrillas had earlier blown up the pipeline which Occidental Petroleum Corp's Cano Limon field, the army said.
An army spokeswoman said it was still not known how the rebels shot the chopper down. The ELN claimed in the past that it had a number of surface-to-air missiles.

The downing of the helicopter was one of the worst rebel attacks since Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) insurgents overran a military base in southern Putumayo province last August, killing 31 soldiers and taking 60 prisoner.
